title: Column comparison for total complexes with finitely many rows
statement: Let C be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], K and L nonnegative double complexes [def-sp-double-complex-total], f:K→L a morphism, and N a natural number. Assume K^{p,q} and L^{p,q} are zero for every p and every q>N. Assume that for every q the horizontal complex map K^{•,q}→L^{•,q}, equivalently the q-th component of the flipped map, is a quasi-isomorphism. Then the canonical total map Tot(f) is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Section 12.25, the second filtration by vertical degree; finite filtration comparison

proof.text: Transpose f so each given horizontal quasi-isomorphism becomes a column map. Extend the inner index then the outer index by zero along embeddingUpNat. Negative coordinates vanish by isZero_extend_X, so hasTotal_of_firstQuadrant gives the integer totals. The outer complexes are strictly ≥0 by extension. For an integer outer degree above N, extendXIso identifies its column with the extension of an original zero column, giving strict ≤N support for both bicomplexes.

In a retained integer degree i≥0 write i as the natural image of q. Outer extendXIso and extendMap_f identify that column map with extendMap of the original flipped q-th column. Mathlib quasiIso_extendMap_iff supplies its quasi-isomorphism. Apply the existing finite-column comparison with bounds 0 and N to get the integer total quasi-isomorphism.

Use the natural arrow isomorphism commuting double-index extension with totalization. Quasi-isomorphism is invariant under this arrow isomorphism; quasiIso_extendMap_iff reflects it back to the natural-indexed flipped total. Finally totalFlipIso with the explicit natural symmetry sign (-1)^(pq) and its coprojection naturality identifies this map with Tot(f).

proof_origin.place: J2 second reading: finite-column comparison applied to the extended transposed bicomplex; only the independent natural extension/totalization arrow isomorphism remains open.
